newsitem.title: USA: Sweeping changes recommended for Los Angeles police.
newsitem.headline: Sweeping changes recommended for Los Angeles police.

text.p: A Los Angeles Police Department report on former Det. Mark Fuhrman's taped allegations of brutality and criminal misconduct recommends sweeping changes in the department, a newspaper said on Tuesday.

The Los Angeles Times said according to a 69-page executive summary of the inqury into Fuhrman's comments, investigators determined that in almost every instance, the now-retired detective was exaggerating or lying about episodes of police brutality, but telling the truth when he spoke of institutional harassment of women on the force.

The Times said the report recommends changes in the way the department handles personnel complaints, disciplines rogue police officers, maintains internal records and holds command officers responsible for the actions of their subordinates.
Released on Monday, the report "contains uncharacteristically candid and critical language for a department document," the Times said.

The investigation was begun because of numerous allegations made by Fuhrman in a series of taped interviews Fuhrman gave to a screenwriter. Fuhrman in the interviews said blacks were often brutally attacked by Los Angeles police officers.
The tapes came to light in the murder trial of O.J. Simpson.
Simpson's defence attorneys used the tapes to show Fuhrman was not telling the truth when he testified he had not used racial slurs in the years prior to Simpson's trial.

The Simpson defence convinced a jury that the case against Fuhrman was flawed and that police, including Fuhrman, may have tampered with evidence to implicate Simpson in the murders of his former wife and her male friend.
Simpson, a former professional football player, was acquitted of the criminal charges, but in a subsequent trial, was ordered to pay millions of dollars in damages for the deaths.
